core_memory.user_schedule: Mondays and Wednesdays are packed with Advanced Algorithms and Distributed Systems. Tuesdays and Thursdays are lighter with Quantum Computing and Game Design. Thursdays also include Philosophy of Mind in the evening. Fridays are open for work on assignments and projects.
core_memory.user_feeling: having a blast, feeling confident, resourceful, and rewarded

archival_memory.user_undergrad_research: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year, and it's been an eye-opening experience. It's given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world, and I'm proud to be part of it. I didn't initially see myself going down the research route, but a professor noticed my skills in bridging technical coding with user experience and encouraged me to apply for a research assistant position in a data visualization lab. I was hesitant at first, but taking the leap turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.user_lab_description: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. We deal with datasets that are tens of terabytes in size. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards. I use advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if dealing with 3D data.
archival_memory.user_first_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. The raw data consisted of daily temperature readings from buoys around the Pacific, scattered across different servers. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to zoom into specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored my first paper on this system, which felt surreal and is one of my proudest moments in college.
archival_memory.user_current_project: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can help scientists gain an intuitive understanding of complex data. By allowing users to interact with 3D representations of data in virtual environments, we can enhance their ability to analyze and explore data in a more immersive and engaging way. This is a departure from traditional data visualization methods, such as looking at raw numerical data in a spreadsheet or using 2D visuals like graphs. The use of VR or AR technologies can provide a more interactive and immersive experience, which can be beneficial for various fields. The project involves experimentation, integration with engines like Unity or Unreal, and efficient data streaming into 3D environments. It's a cutting-edge field, and every day, I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established best-practice library for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.user_research_life: Research life is often misunderstood as me sitting in a quiet corner coding away at a mysterious project. However, it's actually a lot of reading. Academic papers never end, and when trying to solve a bug with rendering volumetric data in VR, I need to comb through conference proceedings or workshops to see if someone has tried something similar. It can get overwhelming, but over time, I've learned how to skim effectively by looking at the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to determine if a paper is relevant. Occasionally, when I discover something interesting, I share it with the rest of the lab, and we discuss how we can incorporate that technique into our workflow.
archival_memory.user_lab_collaboration: I have the opportunity to interact with a group of graduate students in the lab, including master's and PhD students. While it can be intimidating at first, it's also inspiring to see their expertise and dedication to their niche fields. One PhD student has been developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets and is integrating it with our VR platform. This will allow us to display a compressed representation of the data until the user zooms in, enhancing real-time performance. Working alongside him has given me insights into how advanced theoretical concepts are applied in practice. Some of our best brainstorming sessions happen spontaneously, such as in the lab break room, where we discuss ways to offload processing to the GPU while sipping coffee.
archival_memory.user_poster_presentations: We've done a few poster presentations at smaller symposiums around campus, which was a great experience. It requires boiling down complex research into easy-to-digest visuals and talking points. The first time I presented, I was nervous, but it turned out to be a friendly dialogue. People are genuinely interested in what you're doing. There were even a few folks from local startups who showed up, sharing interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. It opened my eyes to how research can transition from academia to real-world applications.
archival_memory.user_publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference(IEEE VIS). Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment in terms of user performance. We conducted a user study with 15 participants, recording their times and gathering UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with each member contributing their expertise: I'm handling the system architecture and prototype design, someone else is writing about the user study methodology, and our PI is weaving it all together. It's a delicate balancing act, especially with my senior coursework and capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.user_grad_school: I'm currently considering whether to pursue a graduate degree. While the idea of contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning is tempting, I'm also interested in seeing how these concepts are applied in real product development. One of my mentors suggested that working in industry for a couple of years can provide a better understanding of the problems that are truly relevant, which could make me a more practical researcher if I decide to pursue a PhD in the future. For now, I'm leaning toward working in the industry and gaining some industry experience before making a decision.
archival_memory.user_frustrations: Research can be frustrating at times. You may spend weeks on an approach that doesn't pan out, or you might discover that your entire idea has already been done and improved upon by a group in Europe or somewhere else. It can feel like a punch in the gut. However, the key is to adapt. We can read that existing paper, incorporate their findings, think of a new angle or application, and push the boundary. That's the essence of research. We're never truly starting from scratch; we're building on the foundation of what others have done. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is something I find really special.
archival_memory.user_lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost vital data that wasn't fully backed up. It was a frantic night of email chains, Zoom calls, and everyone scrambling to see if we could recover the data. We managed to restore most of it, but the crisis highlighted the importance of data backups. After that, we set up a better backup system and implemented checks to ensure we don't rely on a single point of failure again. It was stressful, but it also brought the lab together and taught us a valuable lesson.
archival_memory.user_professor_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student in their class. My PI is very approachable, and I can easily reach out to her for guidance on career direction or for help with challenges in class. She has also been recommending me for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I had the chance to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met experts from around the world who were debating technical details, proposing new frameworks, and sharing their insights. It was fascinating to see the frontier of CS knowledge being explored in real time. These connections have been incredibly valuable and have helped me grow both academically and professionally.
archival_memory.user_journey: My journey in the research world has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that what I do in the lab might shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering could become standard tools, and I'd be proud to say I was part of that from the beginning. The sense of contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. Whether or not I go to grad school soon, this experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. It's enriched my perspective on what it means to be a computer scientist.
